Issued at 1152 AM MDT Fri Oct 30 2026

There is currently moist, southwesterly flow aloft over 
southern Idaho with light showers currently, mainly over our 
western areas. Currently, there is an upper level low centered 
just off the coasts of Washington and Oregon as part of an 
overall trough that extends much farther south to off the coast 
of California, where there is ample sub-tropical moisture 
available. This low/trough is bringing our current moisture and
will drive the weather/precipitation today and the upcoming 
weekend, especially as this low/trough moves over our area late 
Saturday into Sunday. 

Today look for slightly warmer temperatures, compared to 
Thursday, with highs in the 40s for the Central Mountains and 50s
to near 60s for valleys elsewhere. With a trough with moisture
moving into the area today look for wind gusts to begin to
increase, closer to 20-30 mph for many. This will also bring 
some scattered to widespread showers today to the Central 
Mountains and isolated showers for the rest of our area. This 
first round of precipitation will still bring about 0.10 to 0.50
inches of precipitation for the Central mountains and .01 to 
.10 for the rest of the area. Expect snow today mainly in the 
Central mountains, mainly above 7500 feet, with about 1 inch of 
snow expected on Galena Summit today and 2 to 5 inches for 
elevations above 8000 feet. 

Expect patchy to areas of fog Saturday morning and become more 
patchy Sunday and Monday mornings. Precipitation for lower
elevations Saturday still looks to be around 0.10 to 0.10. This
precipitation will likely have some impacts on Halloween 
activities. However, the bulk of the precipitation is still 
arriving later Saturday evening through Sunday and lingering 
into Monday morning. 

By late Saturday into Sunday the low off the Washington coast 
begins to move and makes it way inland aided by an deepening 
trough, which will really picks up more Pacific moisture and 
transports it over southeastern Idaho. This more organized 
round of precipitation will begin in the Central Mountains/Wood 
River Valley/eastern Magic Valley as early as 6 PM Saturday and 
then spread eastward throughout the night. The NBM model is 
still showing about an 90 to 100 percent chance of the entire 
CWA receiving at least 0.25 inch of precipitation with this
system. Precipitation amounts have not changed much from 
the last couple days of model runs. It still seems likely that 
many will see 0.25 to 0.50 inches in the eastern Magic Valley
and Challis area, 0.50 to 0.75 inches in the Snake River Plain 
and lower elevations of the Eastern Highlands and Central 
Mountains. For higher elevations (above 8000 feet) 
precipitation will be pushing 0.80 to 1.50 inches, especially 
for Sun Valley Region, Big Lost Highlands/Copper Basin, Lost 
River Range, and the Montana Divide as well as the Southern 
areas along the Utah border including the Wasatch mountains. 
Temperatures will still be "warm" on Saturday with highs in the 
40s and 50s, but by Sunday our highs will drop into the mid and
upper 30s and 40s. Snow impacts are likely at Galena Summit 
Saturday night into Sunday morning with the forecast still 
showing 4-10" (90th and 10th NBM percentiles with 7 inches being
the 50th percentile) of snow there. A winter weather advisory 
is in effect for the Sun Valley Region and the Big Lost 
Highlands above 7000 feet for Saturday evening through Sunday. 
Elsewhere, the bulk of our snow is expected to remain above most
of the rest of our mountain passes, but that could change 
easily with temperature changes of just a few degrees. Even 
though snow levels will start high, convection can lower snow 
levels, which could drop snow levels to pass levels especially 
for areas like Emigration and Raynolds pass. 

A few showers linger on Monday morning, but we will be drying out 
from west to east by that point and high pressure builds in over the 
area through mid week.
